findings.title: The new exact-equality quote check is a tautology on any honest minter, yet its comment and error name present it as protection against being short-changed
findings.description:
expectedForStable is obtained at :234 from minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount). PhusdStableMinter.mint computes its own phUSDAmount at PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 by calling the SAME public view, with identical arguments, in the SAME transaction, against the same config storage. Neither exchangeRate nor decimals can change between :234 and :251 (both are onlyOwner setters and no path reaches them mid-call). The two sides therefore agree by construction whenever the minter behaves as written, and the check is a no-op on 100% of the honest path.

Its only live effects are (a) Antimatter's phUSD balance changing between the snapshot at :244 and the read at :256 (see CODE-202), and (b) FlaxToken crediting fewer tokens than mint() was asked for (FlaxToken.mint at flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol:58 has no cap and no fee, so this is presently impossible). The comment at :232-233 -- 'Measuring against its own quote, rather than merely against zero, means a short mint cannot pass unnoticed' -- and the error name PhUSDAmountMismatch both read as a slippage/short-mint guard. They are not: there is no caller-supplied minimum, so an owner who lowers exchangeRate still settles an in-flight annihilate at the new rate with the burn already irreversible, and the check passes because it re-quotes at the new rate too. This is ledger F-01 (3aac91383dcb6060, 'no minimum-output guard on an already-irreversible burn') restated -- the new code now LOOKS like the missing guard without being it, which is worse for a future reader than the absence was.
findings.codeSnippet:
:232  // What the minter says it will mint for that deposit. Measuring against its own quote,
:233  // rather than merely against zero, means a short mint cannot pass unnoticed.
:234  uint256 expectedForStable = minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount);
...
:257  if (mintedForStable != expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(expectedForStable, mintedForStable);

-- PhusdStableMinter.sol --
:212  uint256 phUSDAmount = calculateMintAmount(stablecoin, amount);   // same fn, same args, same tx
findings.reachability: ALWAYS on the success path; the check never fires for the reason its comment claims. Not an exploit -- a correctness-of-documentation defect on a security-critical guard.
findings.failureScenario: Owner calls minter.updateExchangeRate(usdc, 0.5e18) while Alice's annihilate(usdc, alice, 100e18) is pending. Alice's tx lands at the new rate: 100 AM burned, 100 USDC pulled, 100 + 50 = 150 phUSD delivered instead of 200. expectedForStable (50e18) equals mintedForStable (50e18), so PhUSDAmountMismatch does not fire and the code reports success. A reader of :232-233 would reasonably believe otherwise.
findings.intentionalityNote: The check does have real (if narrow) value as a defence against a future minter whose mint() diverges from its own quote. The finding is the overstated framing, not the check's presence.
findings.recommendation: Either (i) reword :232-233 to state what the check actually covers ('the minter's mint() must agree with its own calculateMintAmount(); this is NOT a slippage guard'), or (ii) close F-01 properly by adding a `uint256 minPhUSDOut` parameter to annihilate and checking `amount + mintedForStable >= minPhUSDOut` before :260.
findings.poc: reasoning-only (tautology proven by reading PhusdStableMinter.sol:212 vs Antimatter.sol:234)

findings.title: mintedForStable is still a balance DELTA, and exact equality turns any mid-call phUSD arrival into a hard revert of the whole annihilation
findings.description:
mintedForStable at :256 is `_phUSD.balanceOf(this) - phUSDBefore`, an unattributed delta over the window [:244, :256]. Under the old code a windfall in that window was silently forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient (ledger L-01). Under exact equality it now reverts PhUSDAmountMismatch instead. That is the right trade -- a revert beats a silent mis-forward -- but it converts a value-attribution bug into a liveness lever: ONE WEI of phUSD pushed to Antimatter inside the window kills the transaction.

Enumerated actors that can execute code in that window: (1) the `stable` token, at safeTransferFrom :246 and forceApprove :247; (2) PhusdStableMinter, at :251; (3) the registered yield strategy, invoked at PhusdStableMinter.sol:229. All three are owner-registered / first-party. nonReentrant at :221 blocks re-entry into annihilate but does NOT stop any of them from calling phUSD.transfer(antimatter, 1). There is no permissionless lever: Antimatter registers no ERC777/ERC1363 receive hook, and msg.sender is the victim.

Separately, if phUSD were to LEAVE Antimatter in that window the subtraction at :256 underflows and surfaces as an unnamed Panic(0x11) rather than a diagnosable error.
findings.reachability: NOT permissionlessly reachable at c91bc1a. Reachable only by an owner-registered stablecoin, the minter, or the registered yield strategy. Law 3: this is a FOOTGUN, not an exploit -- a competent owner registering an exotic token with a transfer hook would be surprised that a 1-wei phUSD nudge from that token bricks every annihilation for that pair.
findings.failureScenario: PROVEN: test_midCallPhUSDInjectionNowReverts. A registered 18-decimal stablecoin whose _update hook calls phUSD.transfer(antimatter, 1) when it sees a transfer into Antimatter. user calls annihilate(donor, user, 100e18); the call reverts with PhUSDAmountMismatch(100000000000000000000, 100000000000000000001). No annihilation of that stablecoin is ever possible while the hook is live.
findings.footgunTest: Would a competent, non-malicious owner be surprised? YES for the hook case -- the connection between 'this token moves phUSD on transfer' and 'annihilation is permanently bricked' is not obvious from either contract. Suppressed-as-obvious does NOT apply.
findings.recommendation: Bound the tolerance rather than demanding exact equality: `if (mintedForStable < expectedForStable) revert PhUSDAmountMismatch(...)` forwards only expectedForStable and leaves any surplus on the contract for rescueERC20 -- that closes L-01's mis-forward AND removes the brick. If exactness is preferred, document the dependency explicitly in the stablecoin-registration checklist.

findings.title: The new decimals() staticcall copies unbounded return data into memory, so a registered token can make toStableAmount -- and therefore every annihilation of that pair -- cost more gas than a block allows
findings.description:
`(bool ok, bytes memory data) = stable.staticcall(...)` at :292 allocates and RETURNDATACOPYs the callee's ENTIRE return buffer before `data.length != 32` is ever evaluated at :293. Memory expansion is quadratic, so a registered token that answers decimals() with a large blob makes the caller pay for it. The delta introduced this: at 0bb82d8 toStableAmount made no call to `stable` at all, so this is a new liveness dependency on an address Antimatter otherwise never queries.

Two consequences, both new: (a) annihilate() is bricked for that pair, since :230 routes through toStableAmount; (b) toStableAmount is `public view` and the NatSpec added by this same delta at :278-279 explicitly nominates it as an off-chain quote helper ('Off-chain callers using this as a quote helper therefore depend on `stable` being responsive') -- the dependency is acknowledged but the unbounded cost is not. The all-gas-forwarded staticcall reaches the same outcome via a decimals() that simply burns gas (63/64 rule leaves the caller too little to finish).
findings.codeSnippet:
:292  (bool ok, bytes memory data) = stable.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20Metadata.decimals, ()));
:293  if (!ok || data.length != 32) revert DecimalsUnavailable(stable);
findings.reachability: Requires an owner-registered `stable` (the StablecoinNotRegistered guard at :285 correctly runs FIRST, so an arbitrary caller cannot point toStableAmount at a hostile address). The realistic path is an upgradeable registered token whose implementation changes AFTER registration -- outside the owner's control, so this is not an owner-misuse suppression under Law 3. DoS only: fails closed, no theft, no burn (the revert precedes :239).
findings.failureScenario: PROVEN: test_returndataBombGasCost measures a single toStableAmount(bomb, 100e18) at 16,782 gas for a 32-byte answer, 1,815,823 gas for a 640KB answer, and 158,677,386 gas for a 6.4MB answer. test_returndataBombBricksQuote shows the call reverting out-of-gas under a 30,000,000 gas cap against a 64MB answer. Both eth_call quoting and on-chain annihilate for that pair are dead.
findings.recommendation: Read exactly one word and ignore the rest -- an assembly staticcall with a 32-byte output buffer plus an explicit `returndatasize() == 32` check -- and/or cap the forwarded gas (e.g. `{gas: 30000}`), which is ample for any real decimals(). The stated reason for preferring a raw staticcall over try/catch (:289-291, uncatchable uint8 decode of a >255 value) remains valid and is unaffected by this change.

findings.type: new-revert-surface / false-negative on an honest token
findings.title: DecimalsUnavailable also fires on a correctly-registered, honest token whose decimals() is not view-callable, permanently bricking that pair
findings.description: The cross-check reaches `stable` by STATICCALL, which reverts on any state write in the callee. A token that implements decimals() as a non-view function -- one that increments a counter, lazily caches a value, or emits an event -- returns ok == false and is rejected with DecimalsUnavailable even though its registration is correct and its answer would have matched. There is no fallback and no owner override; annihilate for that pair is dead until the token changes. This is the price of the fail-closed design and is arguably the right call, but the NatSpec at :271-279 describes DecimalsUnavailable only as 'a token that does not report usable decimals at all', which does not cover a token that reports perfectly usable decimals through a non-view function.
findings.codeSnippet:
:292  (bool ok, bytes memory data) = stable.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20Metadata.decimals, ()));
:293  if (!ok || data.length != 32) revert DecimalsUnavailable(stable);
findings.reachability: PROVEN reachable in principle; LOW plausibility that any real stablecoin the owner would register is non-view. No loss of funds -- fails closed before the burn at :239.
findings.failureScenario: PROVEN: test_statefulDecimalsBricksHonestToken. A token with `function decimals() public returns (uint8) { reads++; return 18; }` registered with decimals = 18 (correct) reverts DecimalsUnavailable(token) on toStableAmount.
findings.intentionalityNote: Almost certainly intentional fail-closed behaviour. Reported as a documentation/operational-checklist gap, not as a defect in the check.
findings.recommendation: Add non-view decimals() to the stablecoin-registration checklist, and widen the DecimalsUnavailable NatSpec to say 'does not report usable decimals through a static call'.

findings.type: cross-contract residual, root cause out of scope
findings.title: The decimals cross-check protects the Antimatter path only; PhusdStableMinter.mint remains permissionless and still scales by the unverified registered decimals
findings.description: story-002 closes ledger M-01 (a1c81428a47ad295) at Antimatter's entry point: every annihilate routes through toStableAmount at :230, and a registered/actual decimals disagreement now reverts in BOTH directions. But the mis-scaling root cause lives in PhusdStableMinter.calculateMintAmount (PhusdStableMinter.sol:254, `10 ** (18 - config.decimals)`), which is reached directly by the minter's own permissionless `mint(address,uint256)` (PhusdStableMinter.sol:203). Anyone can call that path without touching Antimatter and still mint phUSD against a mis-registered decimals figure. Antimatter cannot fix this from its side; the fix is correct for what Antimatter controls.
findings.reachability: Permissionless via PhusdStableMinter.mint, which is a nested dependency (lib/phUSD-stable-minter) and therefore out of first-party scope for this project. Parked for visibility per Law 1 rather than dropped.
findings.recommendation: Move the cross-check into PhusdStableMinter.registerStablecoin so the invariant is established once, at registration, for every consumer -- not re-derived per-call by each integrator.

deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.label: L-01
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.text: mintedForStable is a balance delta, not an attribution: any phUSD arriving mid-call is forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.verdict: RESOLVED-BY-DELTA (mis-forward), REPLACED BY A NEW LIVENESS COST
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.reasoning: The exact-equality check at :257 converts the silent mis-forward into a hard revert. PROVEN by test_midCallPhUSDInjectionNowReverts: a 1-wei mid-call phUSD arrival now reverts PhUSDAmountMismatch(100e18, 100e18+1) instead of being forwarded to the recipient. The delta itself is unchanged (:256 is still an unattributed delta), but no windfall can now reach the recipient. The residual is filed as CODE-202: the same window is now a brick rather than a leak. NO LEDGER STATUS PROPOSED.

deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.label: L-03
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.text: A near-zero exchangeRate turns a soft throttle into a hard brick
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.reasoning: The zero-quote check moved from :253 (post-burn) to :235 (pre-burn), and the error's NatSpec was rewritten to name the zero-rate cause. The brick is unchanged in substance: an exchangeRate low enough that calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) rounds to 0 still reverts PhUSDNotReceived and makes annihilation of that pair impossible (project test test_zeroExchangeRateReverts at test/Annihilation.t.sol asserts exactly this). It now fails EARLIER and CHEAPER -- before the _burn at :239, before toStableAmount's staticcall has been paid for a second time, and before any state-changing external call -- so the wasted gas on a bricked pair drops materially, and the revert is a named error rather than a post-hoc balance check. Note the pre-burn move does NOT change atomicity: the old placement also reverted the whole tx. It also does nothing for the more damaging non-zero case: a rate of 1 wei still passes both :235 and :257 and settles the caller at a near-total loss on the stable leg (that is F-01/CODE-201 territory, not L-03). NO LEDGER STATUS PROPOSED.

deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.label: Q-02
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.text: recipient guarded against address(0) but not address(this)
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.reasoning: The guard at :223 is byte-identical to 0bb82d8 and still tests only address(0). recipient == address(this) still routes _phUSD.mint(this, amount) at :260 and a self-transfer at :261, stranding the full 2x output on Antimatter for rescueERC20. Checked for a NEW interaction with the c91bc1a delta and found none: both credits occur strictly AFTER the :256 read and the :257 check, so a self-recipient cannot perturb mintedForStable within its own call, and on a SUBSEQUENT call the stranded balance is captured symmetrically by phUSDBefore at :244. The one thing the delta did change is who can be named: with the `from` parameter gone, a self-recipient can only ever strand the CALLER's own value, never a third party's. NO LEDGER STATUS PROPOSED.

deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.label: Q-01
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.text: toStableAmount is a decimals-only rescale and is not a phUSD preview; local `decimals` shadows ERC20.decimals()
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.verdict: UNAFFECTED IN SUBSTANCE, AGGRAVATED IN FRAMING
deltaReconciliationOfOpenRun01Findings.reasoning: Both halves survive verbatim. (1) The shadow is still there: `uint8 decimals` is declared at :284 inside a contract that inherits ERC20.decimals(); the delta added lines around it without renaming it, and the new error DecimalsMismatch(address,uint8,uint256) now propagates that shadowed local into an ABI-visible parameter. (2) The function still returns a stablecoin quantity and still tells the caller nothing about the phUSD they would receive -- it never touches exchangeRate. The delta's new NatSpec at :278-279 ('Off-chain callers using this as a quote helper therefore depend on `stable` being responsive') now POSITIVELY ENDORSES using it as a quote helper, which is precisely the misreading Q-01 warned about, and it does so without saying what it does not quote. Per the standing principle that falsely-exhaustive in-source docs raise rather than lower severity, the new NatSpec makes Q-01 marginally worse, not better. NO LEDGER STATUS PROPOSED.

A_annihilateFrom_to_annihilate.verdict: CLEAN - no dangling references, no consumer breakage

checks.check: any remaining reference to the 4-arg signature anywhere in the repo, its docs, or its nested dependencies
checks.result: ZERO hits. `grep -rl annihilateFrom .` over the whole tree including lib/ returns nothing. CLAUDE.md (3 sites), test/Annihilation.t.sol and test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol were all updated in the same commits.

checks.check: an ERC20 allowance surface on Antimatter that now confers nothing a holder would expect
checks.result: NOT A DEFECT. approve/allowance/transferFrom remain, and after the delta they mean exactly and only what they mean on any ERC20 -- which is the point of the fix. There is no residual function that reads _allowances for a purpose other than transferFrom: `_spendAllowance` has zero occurrences in src/. The project test test_antimatterAllowanceGrantsNoPowerOverHolder asserts a max allowance now confers nothing (it reverts on the spender's own empty balance).

NO BREAKAGE. Only the parameter NAME changed; the type list is unchanged (address,address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256), so topic0 is byte-identical and the indexed layout is unchanged. Semantically the second topic narrowed from 'the debited holder' to 'the caller', but under the new code those are always the same address, so an indexer filtering the second topic by a holder address gets an identical result set. The only genuine loss is historical: pre-delta logs where caller != from would now be misread, and there are none because the contract is not deployed.

checks.check: selector change breaking a deployed integrator
checks.result: NON-ISSUE. `annihilateFrom(address,address,address,uint256)` and `annihilate(address,address,uint256)` are different selectors, but the repo contains no script/, no broadcast/, no deployment records and no addresses -- Antimatter is pre-deployment, so there is no on-chain caller to break.

checks.check: the CLAUDE.md burn-denylist invariant test still guards the right thing
checks.result: PARTIAL - already filed. test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints still enumerates four literal signatures, one of which (`annihilate(address,uint256)`) is now a near-miss of the real entry point and is explicitly annotated as such. Re-introducing a burn-on-behalf entry point under any other name would not be caught. This is exactly ledger F-02 (78612be9264d2b49, 'a four-name denylist, not an invariant check') and is not re-filed.

B_decimals_crosscheck.verdict: SOUND core, three residuals filed (CODE-203, CODE-204, CODE-205)

checks.check: return-data length semantics; a token returning >32 bytes
checks.result: CORRECT but COSTLY. `data.length != 32` rejects both short and long answers before any decode, so there is no truncation or misread. The cost of getting there is unbounded -> CODE-203.

CORRECT AND DELIBERATE. abi.decode(data,(uint256)) on exactly 32 bytes cannot revert. Decoding as uint8 would have made a >255 answer revert inside the ABI decoder in the CALLER's frame, which try/catch cannot intercept -- the comment at :289-291 states this correctly. A value of 300 instead surfaces as DecimalsMismatch(stable, 6, 300) (project test test_toStableAmountRevertsOnDecimalsAboveUint8Range). The uint256 widening is also what makes a USDT-style `uint256 public decimals` work (project test test_toStableAmountAcceptsUint256ReturningToken). No defect.

checks.check: check ordering vs the pre-existing guards
checks.result: CORRECT. StablecoinNotRegistered (:285) and UnsupportedDecimals (:286) both run BEFORE the external call, so an unregistered/arbitrary address can never make Antimatter staticcall it. This is what keeps CODE-203 owner-gated rather than permissionless.

checks.check: gas griefing / 63-64 rule on a view called in a state-changing path AND exposed as a public quote helper
checks.result: REAL -> CODE-203. Measured: 158.7M gas for one toStableAmount against a 6.4MB decimals() answer.

checks.check: new revert surface for off-chain integrators and on-chain callers
checks.result: REAL. toStableAmount went from a pure config read to an externally-call-dependent function with two new revert modes (DecimalsUnavailable, DecimalsMismatch). The NatSpec acknowledges the dependency at :278-279 but understates DecimalsUnavailable -> CODE-204.
HANDLED. staticcall to a codeless address returns ok == true with zero-length data, which :293 rejects as DecimalsUnavailable (project test test_toStableAmountRevertsOnCodelessStable).

checks.check: a token that answers a different value on a later call (inconsistent within a tx)
checks.result: RESIDUAL, NOT FILED. Antimatter reads decimals() once at :292; PhusdStableMinter re-reads its own config.decimals (never the token) at :254. So Antimatter's cross-check binds only its own reading. A token that answers honestly once and dishonestly thereafter cannot exploit this, because both scalings use the MINTER's registered figure, not the token's answer -- the token's answer is only ever used as a veto. Correct by construction.

C_pre_quote_and_exact_equality.verdict: NARROWER THAN ADVERTISED (CODE-201) and a new brick lever (CODE-202)

divergenceSourcesEnumerated.reason: PhusdStableMinter.sol:221 is a require, never a haircut, and config.mintedToday is written at :222 AFTER phUSDAmount is computed at :212. A cap over-run reverts inside minter.mint at Antimatter.sol:251 and never reaches :257.

Both are reverts (PhusdStableMinter.sol:204, :209). toStableAmount discarding config.enabled (Antimatter.sol:284, profile INV-11) means a disabled stablecoin survives the pre-quote and dies inside minter.mint -- a revert, not a divergence.
updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner and no path from :234 to :251 reaches it. Both sides re-quote at whatever rate is live, which is precisely why the check is a tautology -> CODE-201.

divergenceSourcesEnumerated.source: mid-call phUSD ARRIVAL at Antimatter (between :244 and :256)
divergenceSourcesEnumerated.reason: The only genuine divergence source. mintedForStable is a delta, so an arrival inflates it. Reachable ONLY by the stable token's hooks (:246/:247), the minter (:251) or the yield strategy (PhusdStableMinter.sol:229) -- all owner-configured. PROVEN -> CODE-202.
Same window, opposite sign; underflows at :256 into an unnamed Panic(0x11) instead of PhUSDAmountMismatch. Same owner-gated reachability. Noted inside CODE-202.
Would diverge, but phUSD is FlaxToken (flax-token-v2/src/FlaxToken.sol), a plain OZ ERC20 with no rebase, no fee and no hooks. NOT REACHABLE at c91bc1a. FoT is a C4 known-invalid class in any case.
FlaxToken.mint (:58-69) checks authorization and mintVersion then calls _mint with the full amount -- no cap, no fee. NOT REACHABLE today; this is the one future-proofing the check genuinely buys.

nonReentrant at :221 blocks it (project test test_reentrantStableIsBlocked, mock test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol). Correctly noted that the guard does NOT stop `stable` from calling OTHER contracts during :246 -- which is exactly the CODE-202 path.

C_pre_quote_and_exact_equality.law3Verdict: The registered-stablecoin-is-owner-chosen assumption makes CODE-202 a FOOTGUN, not an invalid finding. It is not 'a malicious owner could' -- the owner registering a token with a phUSD-touching transfer hook is a non-obvious configuration whose consequence (permanent brick of that pair) a competent operator would not anticipate. It IS correctly out of exploit territory: no theft, no partial settlement, and the burn at :239 is unwound by the revert.

reentrancyClassChecklist.evidence: Strict CEI reconfirmed at c91bc1a: the sole local state write is _burn(msg.sender, amount) at :239, and it precedes every state-changing external call (:246, :247, :251, :253, :260, :261). Nothing in Antimatter storage is written after :239. annihilate is nonReentrant (:221). The delta MOVED two checks (:234, :235) to before the burn, which strengthens this.

nonReentrant at :221 uses OZ ReentrancyGuard's single contract-wide _status slot, so no external call in the window can re-enter annihilate. Project test test_reentrantStableIsBlocked + test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol (updated to the 3-arg signature in commit c91bc1a) exercise the hostile-_update path. Independently reconfirmed by this scan: the mock re-entry reverts ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall.

The unguarded state-mutating siblings are mint(address,uint256) (:197, onlyApprovedMinters -- owner or an owner-approved contract) and the inherited ERC20 mutators (transfer/approve/transferFrom). Re-entering mint during annihilate's external-call window would mint AM, but the caller must already be an owner-approved principal (Law 3, trusted). Re-entering transfer/approve reads no stale value, because _burn at :239 has already settled _balances and _totalSupply before the first external call -- there is no window in which annihilate has taken value without recording it. rescueERC20 (:306) is onlyOwner AND nonReentrant.

Antimatter's public views are the ERC20 set (name/symbol/decimals/totalSupply/balanceOf/allowance), the minter-set getters, phUSD()/phUSDMinter(), and toStableAmount. toStableAmount reads NO Antimatter storage at all -- only minter config and the token's decimals -- so it cannot be read mid-flight in an inconsistent state. The ERC20 views ARE transiently inconsistent between :239 and :260/:261: totalSupply and balanceOf(msg.sender) are already decremented while the corresponding phUSD does not yet exist, and external code runs in that window at :246/:247/:251. Nothing in this repo or its dependencies prices off Antimatter.totalSupply(), so there is no victim today -> parked as MR-02-01.
No ERC721 anywhere in src/. No _safeMint / safeTransferFrom / onERC721Received.

phUSD (FlaxToken) is a plain OZ ERC20 with no hooks. `stable` could be ERC777, but Antimatter registers no ERC1820 interface so no tokensReceived fires on it, and the sender at :246 is msg.sender (the victim), who would have to register a hook against themselves. Any code an ERC777 stable does run is the same untrusted-code window already covered by nonReentrant and by CODE-202.

manualReviewItems.title: Transiently deflated Antimatter.totalSupply() between the burn (:239) and the phUSD mint (:260)
manualReviewItems.reason: Read-only-reentrancy shape with no victim in the current codebase. Between :239 and :260 the AM supply has fallen while the offsetting phUSD has not yet been created, and untrusted code (the `stable` token, the yield strategy) executes inside that window. If any future contract -- a backing-ratio oracle, an AM/phUSD TWAP, a collateral valuer -- ever reads Antimatter.totalSupply(), it becomes exploitable from that window. Parked rather than filed because no such consumer exists at c91bc1a.
manualReviewItems.action: Re-check on any commit that introduces an on-chain consumer of Antimatter.totalSupply() or balanceOf.

summary.highlights: The delta is well constructed and closes the run-01 High (H-01) and Medium (M-01) at the Antimatter boundary. No new High or Medium. The three residuals worth a reader's attention are: (1) CODE-201 -- the new exact-equality check is a tautology on any honest minter, but its comment presents it as a short-mint guard, which risks a future reader believing F-01's missing minimum-output guard has been supplied; (2) CODE-202 -- exact equality turns a mid-call phUSD arrival from a silent mis-forward (L-01) into a permanent brick, PROVEN with a passing PoC, owner-gated and therefore a footgun rather than an exploit; (3) CODE-203 -- the new decimals() staticcall copies unbounded return data, measured at 158.7M gas for a 6.4MB answer, which is a new liveness dependency on the registered token that did not exist at 0bb82d8.
summary.confidenceNote: CODE-202, CODE-203 and CODE-204 are each reproduced by a named, passing, audit-authored test in workspace/antimatter/test/audit/Tier2Delta.t.sol. CODE-201 and CODE-205 are reasoning-only and are stated as such.
